project.title: FrinStore
project.subtitle: Local Ice Cream Online Marketplace Platform
project.elevatorPitch: A web platform where customers browse FrinStore ice cream products online, place orders with checkout and payments, track orders, and where staff manage inventory and sales through an admin dashboard.
problemStatements: Customers cannot conveniently browse ice cream products, flavors, and availability without visiting the physical store.
Manual ordering through chat or phone causes order errors, delays, and poor tracking of customer purchases.
The store has no centralized system for managing inventory, orders, and sales reporting.

rationale: Frequent testing reduces large late failures

included: Admin dashboard for inventory and sales

functionalRequirements: Product browsing and search by flavor, price, or category
nonFunctionalRequirements: Initial load within ~3 seconds under normal traffic
Support for at least 500 concurrent users (target)
Encryption for customer and payment data
Secure authentication and role-based access control
Database backups at least every 24 hours

packages.name: frinstore_frontend
packages.description: Vue 3 single-page application (customer storefront + admin routes).

packages.name: frinstore_backend
packages.description: Python environment scaffold for the REST API service (implementation per design phase).

packages.name: react_prototype
packages.description: Optional early UI prototype (not the primary production frontend).

techStack.summary: Vue 3 SPA with Pinia talks to a FastAPI + SQLite backend (JWT). Payment methods are recorded only — no live gateway in this build.

backend.auth: JWT access tokens (Bearer) + password hashing (e.g., bcrypt or argon2)
backend.payments: Provider SDK or hosted checkout (align with GCash/card requirements from SRS)
backend.observability: Structured logging; optional OpenAPI docs auto-generated from FastAPI

devOps.hostingStrategy: Cloud hosting for API + database; static hosting or CDN for frontend build artifacts
devOps.ciSuggestion: Lint + typecheck + unit tests on pull requests

architecture.communication: HTTPS JSON REST between browser and API
principles: Repository or data-access layer isolating SQL
architecture.highLevelDiagram: Client (Vue SPA) → API Gateway / Reverse Proxy → Python API → Relational DB; Payment provider called server-side only.

directories.purpose: HTTP routers grouped by domain (auth, products, orders, admin).

domainModules: Admin inventory and basic sales summaries
Notifications (email or SMS adapter — can start as queued jobs or simple transactional sends)

implementationStatus.note: Implemented: FastAPI app under frinstore_backend/app with SQLite (frinstore.db), JWT auth, product CRUD, customer checkout orders (stock decrement), and admin order status updates. Seed creates catalog + admin@frinstore.com / admin123. Run: uvicorn app.main:app --reload from frinstore_backend.
implementationStatus.livePaymentGateway: Excluded per project scope — payment method is stored for fulfillment only.

architecture.state: Pinia store; JWT in localStorage; cart persisted locally; catalog and orders loaded from API.
architecture.navigation: Declarative routes with navigation guards for authentication and roles
architecture.apiIntegration: src/lib/api.ts calls FastAPI (/api/*) with Bearer token; checkout requires authenticated customer.

directories.purpose: App bootstrap: Vue app, Pinia, router.
Global application state (user, catalog, cart, orders).
Route-level views (Home, Products, Cart, Checkout, Orders, Login, Register, Profile, About).
Shared layout and UI building blocks.
Reusable UI primitives (Button, Card, toast wrapper).
REST client + response mapping (snake_case API → frontend domain types).
Legacy seed list (catalog now served from API; kept for reference).
localStorage keys and client persistence helpers.

keyUserJourneys: Browse catalog → product detail → add to cart → checkout → order confirmation
Admin login → manage products and orders

browserStandards: Accessibility baseline via semantic HTML and Headless UI patterns

standardsAndConventions.api: REST + JSON; plural nouns for resources; consistent error envelope
standardsAndConventions.security: HTTPS; HttpOnly cookies or Bearer tokens (team choice documented in SRS); never expose secret keys in frontend bundles
standardsAndConventions.formatting: Prettier/ESLint optional additions for team consistency
